answer: Before an agent can post orders, it must lock a scarce token in a public kernel contract; the token stays locked while its orders are active and is forfeited if the agent provably double-spends or breaks a signed commitment. This does not prove one person controls one identity, but it makes Sybil influence costly: an attacker must buy and immobilize separate tokens for each fake agent, tying up capital that could otherwise fund real activity. A velvet name or comet-bright profile cannot bypass the bond.
